Automated Model Briefing

⚠ AI-generated text — may be wrong, incomplete, or overconfident. This is automated commentary on experimental model output, not flight advice and not a weather forecast. It has not been reviewed by a meteorologist.

Overall Assessment A mixed day with strong thermals at some sites but sharp lapse rates requiring advanced skills. Afternoon SW winds increase markedly, creating gusty conditions at ridge launches. Significant overdevelopment risk at Daydreams, Hallelujah, and Rainbow Ridge will limit usable hours; best soaring windows are morning through early afternoon at the most sheltered thermic sites.

Site Breakdown

  • Kingsbury grade: Favorable – early morning thermal window before winds turn SW and strong. Fly 9am–11am; peak w* 416 ft/min, thermal ceiling 3868 ft AGL. Sharp thermals (lapse rate 8.8 °C/km), advanced pilots only.
  • Hallelujah: Marginal – PM window with SW flow but overdevelopment risk 36% and sharp lapse rate. Fly 12pm–3pm; peak w* 524 ft/min, thermal ceiling 5442 ft AGL. Sharp thermals (10.0 °C/km), advanced pilots only.
  • Slide Mountain: Marginal – crosswind all day and low thermal ceiling. Brief early flyable 8am–10am in lighter crosswind; peak w* 387 ft/min, ceiling 1699 ft AGL.
  • McClellan: Favorable – light winds and strong thermals within preferred direction. Fly 10am–1pm; peak w* 602 ft/min, thermal ceiling 6480 ft AGL. Sharp thermals (10.1 °C/km), advanced pilots only.
  • West McClellan: Marginal – afternoon SW flow builds quickly; usable window 1pm–3pm before gusts exceed 30 mph. Peak w* 526 ft/min, ceiling 4742 ft AGL. Sharp thermals (9.9 °C/km), advanced pilots only.
  • Peavine Mountain: Unfavorable – strong SW winds 25–34 mph and gusts to 34 mph all day exceed safe ridge-soaring limits.
  • Rainbow Ridge: Marginal – strong thermals but persistent crosswind and 50% overdevelopment risk. Fly 12pm–2pm for best lift; peak w* 615 ft/min, ceiling 7107 ft AGL. Sharp thermals (10.1 °C/km), advanced pilots only.
  • Duck Hill: Marginal – crosswind all day despite good thermal strength. Afternoon window 12pm–3pm; peak w* 520 ft/min, ceiling 4767 ft AGL. Sharp thermals (9.5 °C/km), advanced pilots only.
  • Daydreams: Unfavorable – 95% overdevelopment, extensive cloud cover will shade the hill. Sharp thermals (8.5 °C/km) but unusable due to OD.

Hazards

  • Overdevelopment: Daydreams (95% of flying hours), Rainbow Ridge (50%), Hallelujah (36%) – widespread clouds suppress lift.
  • Low-level wind shear: Hazardous layer speed shear ≥5 mph at Kingsbury (5 mph at 249 ft AGL), Slide Mountain (6 mph at 242 ft AGL), Rainbow Ridge (6 mph at 6576 ft AGL), Duck Hill (6 mph at 3700 ft AGL), Daydreams (6 mph at 4099 ft AGL).
  • Rotor turbulence possible downwind of Peavine Mountain and the Carson Range due to strong SW flow.
  • Sharp thermals: Lapse rate >8 °C/km at Kingsbury, Hallelujah, McClellan, West McClellan, Rainbow Ridge, Duck Hill, Daydreams – suitable only for advanced/expert pilots.

Site Forecast ?Top of Thermals (PBLH) — height of the turbulent mixing layer; thermals typically reach this ceiling.
LCL (Lifted Condensation Level) — altitude where rising air reaches its dew point; theoretical cloud base.
Cloud Base — lowest model level with >10% cloud fraction.
w* — convective velocity scale; higher = stronger thermals (ft/min).
Cloud Cover — max cloud fraction over the column (0–100%).
Wind thresholds: orange = 12 mph, red = 18 mph.
